# Answer record — Sam Okafor (fictional test subject)

Interview date: 2026-07-13. Subject: freelance UX researcher + part-time design instructor, works solo, ships research reports and workshop decks. **Stakes note: MEDIUM** (client work, reversible outputs, no production systems).

## Dial settings (readback-confirmed unless marked)

- **D1 Task/project threshold** — by time: anything past a half-day gets a plan. *(E1: "If it's a morning's work I just do it; a multi-day study, I write a brief first.")*
- **D2 Approval boundary** — balanced (Critical asks; High reports-after).
- **D3 Deletion authority** — owner-only, per category. *(E1: "Delete drafts freely; never delete a client's raw data without me.")*
- **D4 Approval scope** — one approval = one instance (default; no strong signal).
- **D5 Journaling depth** — high/critical only. *(E1: "I don't want a diary of every edit.")*
- **D6 Metadata richness** — minimal (dates only).
- **D7 Backup stack depth** — standard (checkpoint + remote).
- **D8 Portability strictness** — pragmatic (Figma and Notion allowed; exports named).
- **D9 Handoff depth** — lightweight status note.
- **D10 AI autonomy posture** — report-first on everything consequential (default).
- **D11 Report style** — terse bullets; recommendations mandatory. *(E1: "Tell me what you'd do, don't make me pick from a menu.")*

## Evidence-graded stories

- **E1** (raw first-person): "I lost two weeks of interview notes once when my laptop died — no backup. Never again." *(Backup motivation.)*
- **E4** (observed): asked to show a current off-machine backup — none existed on interview day. **Stated-vs-observed gap:** wants reliable backup, doesn't yet have one.

## Personal rule that fits no dial

- Client raw data (recordings, transcripts) lives in the client's own space, never in Sam's estate. *(Hard privacy line — goes in the pack's own principles, labeled theirs.)*
